coverage.bullet: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds at the repo root and `pnpm -r typecheck` exits 0 across apps/api and packages/contracts.
`docker compose up postgres api-migrate api` results in `api` reporting healthy on `/api/health`, with `api-migrate` exiting 0 before `api` starts.

POST /api/auth.login with valid seeded credentials returns HTTP 200, sets HttpOnly+Secure `session` and `refresh_token` cookies plus a non-HttpOnly `csrf_token` cookie, and returns `{ user: { id, email, role } }`; invalid credentials return HTTP 401 with `{ error: { code: "UNAUTHORIZED" } }` and no cookies.
POST /api/auth.refresh rotates the refresh token (old hash revoked, new hash stored); a replayed refresh cookie returns HTTP 401.
GET /api/auth.me returns the current user on a valid session cookie and HTTP 401 otherwise; POST /api/auth.logout clears both cookies and revokes the active refresh-token row.
Any state-changing route invoked without a matching `X-CSRF-Token` header to the `csrf_token` cookie returns HTTP 403 with `{ error: { code: "FORBIDDEN" } }`.

An integration test attempting login with an unknown email still incurs an argon2id verify (constant-time path) — asserted by a Vitest spy on the injected `verify` dependency confirming it was called exactly **once** in both the unknown-email and wrong-password paths.
A log-capture integration test asserts no API log line emitted during auth flows contains a password, JWT, refresh token, or CSRF token value.

The `refresh_token` table is created in the initial migration with these columns: `id uuid pk default gen_random_uuid()`, `user_id uuid not null references user(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`, `token_hash text not null unique`, `family_id uuid not null`, `replaced_by_id uuid null references refresh_token(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`, `expires_at timestamptz not null`, `revoked_at timestamptz null`, `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`. Hashing uses sha256 of the raw token (cheap, deterministic, indexed via the `unique` constraint on `token_hash`).

Refresh rotation is wrapped in a single Postgres transaction that begins with `SELECT ... FROM refresh_token WHERE token_hash = $1 FOR UPDATE`; the winner sets `revoked_at = now()` and `replaced_by_id` on the old row, inserts a new row carrying the same `family_id`, and commits. Two concurrent refresh requests against the same cookie are asserted by integration test to produce exactly one HTTP 200 with a new token pair and exactly one HTTP 401 — the loser hits a row whose `revoked_at` is already set inside the locked read and returns 401 without issuing tokens.

On a replay against an already-revoked row (the `FOR UPDATE` read finds a row with non-null `revoked_at`), the service treats this as theft: it UPDATEs every `refresh_token` row sharing the offending row's `family_id` to set `revoked_at = now()`, returns HTTP 401, and emits a single `level=warn` log line containing `userId`, `familyId`, and `requestId`. An integration test presents a previously-rotated refresh cookie and asserts (a) the response is 401, (b) every row in that `family_id` has non-null `revoked_at`, (c) exactly one `warn` log line is captured with those three fields.

POST /api/auth.login enforces a per-IP+email sliding-window rate limit of 5 attempts per 15 minutes, implemented in-memory inside the auth module (no Redis, no DB). The 6th attempt within the window returns HTTP 429 with `{ error: { code: "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS" } }` and a `Retry-After` header; successful logins do NOT reset the counter (only the window expiry does). Asserted by an integration test that fires 6 sequential bad logins against the same email + simulated IP and confirms the 6th returns 429.

POST /api/auth.logout is idempotent: it returns HTTP 204 unconditionally, clears the `session`, `refresh_token`, and `csrf_token` cookies whether or not they were present, and revokes the matching `refresh_token` row (sets `revoked_at = now()`) only if the presented cookie hashes to an existing non-revoked row. An integration test asserts a logout with no cookies returns 204 with `Set-Cookie` clearing headers and no DB writes, and a logout with a valid refresh cookie returns 204 and flips that row's `revoked_at`.

The initial migration creates a minimal `user(id uuid pk default gen_random_uuid(), email citext unique not null, role text not null check (role in ('patient','doctor')), created_at timestamptz not null default now(), deleted_at timestamptz null)` table inside `apps/api/src/modules/auth/schema.ts`; downstream `accounts` will adopt and extend this table when that feature lands (no rename / no second user table).
gates: rg --quiet -i 'CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS citext' apps/api/src/db/migrations/0000_init.sql

coverage.bullet: JWT signing uses HS256 with a `JWT_SECRET` environment variable; `apps/api` boot fails fast with a clear error if `JWT_SECRET` is missing or shorter than 32 bytes (asserted by a startup test that loads the bootstrap module with an undersized secret and expects a thrown error).

The seed runs inline at the end of the `api-migrate` one-shot container (`drizzle-kit migrate && node dist/seed/main.js`); the seed is idempotent (re-running on a populated DB inserts zero rows and exits 0), asserted by an integration test that runs the seed twice against the same container.

The seed inserts at least one doctor and at least one patient. All seeded users share a single password (literal value loaded from a `SEED_PASSWORD` env var, default `"medbridge-dev"` for local compose only) but each has a distinct email (`doctor1@medbridge.local`, `patient1@medbridge.local`, …). The same password across roles is intentional for dev ergonomics and is documented in `.env.example` with a `# dev only — never reuse in any non-local environment` comment.
